title: Algebraic Degree of n-th Roots: Non-Perfect-Power Criterion (OQ-03)
description: Proves: if m has a prime factor p with p | m but p² ∤ m, then X^n - m is irreducible over ℚ (Eisenstein criterion), minpoly ℚ (m^(1/n)) = X^n - m, and [ℚ(m^(1/n)) : ℚ] = n. 12 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The irrationality of ∛2 follows from [ℚ(∛2):ℚ] = 3 (Eisenstein's criterion). This file generalizes: any n-th root of a non-perfect-power has algebraic degree exactly n.
overview.problemStatement: Prove: for m with square-free prime factor p (p | m, p² ∤ m) and n ≥ 2, the extension [ℚ(m^(1/n)):ℚ] = n.
overview.proofStrategy: Eisenstein criterion at prime p: X^n - m satisfies the conditions (p | -m = constant term, p ∤ leading coeff = 1, p² ∤ m). Irreducibility → minpoly = X^n - m → degree = n.
keyInsights: **Eisenstein at p**: X^n - m is irreducible over ℚ when p | m and p² ∤ m. This is Eisenstein's criterion with the 'right' prime p.
**Non-perfect-power connection**: if m = k^n for some integer k, then v_p(m) = n·v_p(k) ≥ n ≥ 2 for any prime p | k. Conversely, having v_p(m) = 1 means m is not a perfect n-th power.
**Examples**: ∛6, ∛10, ⁵√12, ∜30 all have algebraic degree equal to the root (Eisenstein at p = 2 or 3 respectively).

sections.title: Eisenstein Irreducibility and Algebraic Degree
sections.summary: X^n - m irreducible (Eisenstein). minpoly_eq_Xn_sub_m. field_extension_degree_eq_n. concrete examples: ∛6, ∛10, ⁵√12.
sections.mathContext: $[\mathbb{Q}(m^{1/n}) : \mathbb{Q}] = n$ when $\exists p$ prime: $p \mid m$, $p^2 \nmid m$.

conclusion.summary: 12 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Algebraic degree = n for non-perfect-power n-th roots proved via Eisenstein's criterion.
conclusion.implications: This result cleanly characterizes when n-th roots are algebraically independent — exactly the non-perfect-power condition.
openQuestions: Can the result be extended to n-th roots over arbitrary number fields?
Can the algebraic degree be computed for composite radicals like ∛2 + ∛3?
Can Eisenstein's criterion be formalized for p-adic irreducibility?
